narrative: OMX30 faces conflicting signals ahead of Friday open. While continental Europe rallies (+0.55-0.59%), North America weakness and Asia selloff (-0.6% to -1.93%) create a fragmented global backdrop. US 10Y yields spiked 221bp—historically supportive for Swedish banks via NIM expansion—but negative for real estate capex and tech DCF valuations. Technical picture is cautious: the index sits +5.1% above 200-MA (structurally bullish) but trades -0.1% below 50-MA with MACD below signal and ADX only 20.0 (weak directional conviction). The Stochastic K=15.1 is deeply oversold, signaling potential mean-reversion bounce intraday, but RSI 41.2 remains neutral. FX headwind: EUR/SEK +0.70% pressures export margin upside.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens Friday with modest bullish bias on European sector momentum offset by conflicting macro signals. Europe's +0.5% avg against US -0.6% and Asia -1.3% avg creates a defensive tilt; expect opening range 3105-3135 around yesterday's 3123 close. Banks (SEB, Handelsbanken) should outperform on 10Y yields +221bp, but watch real estate (Balder, Castellum) for refinancing concern signals. Exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) benefit from USD/SEK +1.02% but tech sentiment remains soft on NASDAQ -0.65%; keep Ericsson/Hexagon on watch for sector rotation risk. Boliden supported by copper +1.12% and gold +0.47%—relative outperformer. Oil -3.33% removes headwind for industrials. Key technical watch: Stochastic K=15.1 is oversold (mean reversion bounce likely intraday), but ADX 20.0 warns trend is weak; stay disciplined on support 3085, resistance 3180.
